sn46.1:1.2: For the “dragon” (_nāga_) see [sn29.1:1.1]() and notes. | The root etymological sense of _nāga_ seems to be “naked”, from where it was applied to hairless animals such as the “snake”, especially the cobra, and the elephant. It is also connected with that naked feature of the earth, the mountain (_naga_). That which belongs to the mountain is the _nāga_, the “dragon”; the primordial serpent Vṛtra coiled around the mountain ([sn2.3:3.4]()). _Nāga_ is also a term for hill tribes. The snake, elephant, and mountain are all powerful, and their nakedness emphasizes their independence. This, it seems, informed the cluster of meanings behind applying _nāga_ to the shaven-headed and spiritually mighty “giants”, the arahants.
sn46.1:1.4: The seven awakening factors especially emphasize the emotional and holistic dimension of meditative growth. Unlike the eightfold path, they do not explicitly include the factor of ethics, but this passage shows that ethics is their foundation.
sn46.1:1.9: “Rapture” (_pīti_) is a joyous emotional response to pleasure, usually a spiritual sense of elevation or uplift in meditation.
